# aussiefy

Rewrites plain English as Australian slang, with level \(1\-5, `tourist` to `swaggie`),
vulgarity \(0\-3, `nan` to `tradie`) and embellishment \(0\-2, deadset/dinkum/troppo\) controls. Now, a deterministic, seeded rule engine
does the translating from a YAML slang dictionary. Stone the flamin' crows, any agent can use its CLI or MCP toolkit to write and
check richer retellings; optional model\-assisted modes can run that work for ya.

```
$ aussiefy "I'm extremely busy." -l 4 -s 7
I'm flat out like a lizard drinking.
```

## Install

Requires Python 3.10\+. Well, these commands install the `v0.2.0` release. Releases are on `main`;
development continues on `dev`. A full commit SHA can be used in place of the tag.

```sh
pip install "git+https://github.com/underware-gg/aussiefy@v0.2.0"            # core
pip install "aussiefy[llm] @ git+https://github.com/underware-gg/aussiefy@v0.2.0"   # + built-in API modes
```

Anyway, other extras: `mcp` (the `aussiefy-mcp` server\), `embeddings`, `scrape`, `dev`. For development, clone the
repo and `pip install -e '.[dev]'`.

The CLI toolkit, portable skill and MCP server work with yer chosen agent without an API key for aussiefy.
Use the same workflow from Claude, Codex or another agent with shell or MCP access. See
[agent integration](docs/user/agents.md) for skill discovery'n tools, and
[model-assisted modes](docs/user/llm-modes.md) for writin' workflows'n the optional API client's setup.
Ya can point yer agent at [the portable skill](skills/aussiefy/SKILL.md); it explains the CLI
workflow'n links to setup instructions.

## Usage

```sh
aussiefy "Are you crazy?"                        # translate at level 5 (swaggie)
aussiefy story.txt -l 3 --vulgarity nan          # a file, level 3, no swearing
echo "I'm exhausted." | aussiefy -l 4 -s random  # stdin, a random seed (printed to stderr)
aussiefy "Are you crazy?" --explain              # explain every decision
aussiefy yarn story.txt                          # optional built-in API client (needs [llm])
```

```python
from aussiefy import translate

translate("I'm extremely busy.", level=4, seed=7).text
```

The rule engine gives the same output for the same text, dials, settings'n seed. See [docs/README.md](docs/README.md) for the full
documentation: guides, every command, the dictionary, yarn mode, the MCP server'n how the engine works.
